reason: The narrative explicitly portrays the Israelites complaining (murmuring/lilonu) against Moses and Aaron regarding God's plan. This complaint is presented as sinful rebellion, resulting in severe divine punishment: all adults (except Caleb and Joshua) will die in the wilderness. The text demonstrates that murmuring against leadership is morally wrong and brings judgment. However, this statement somewhat oversimplifies the passage's primary moral, which centers on faithlessness and lack of trust in God's power and promises, even after witnessing miracles. The complaint is ultimately against God's plan rather than mere personal grievance against leaders' character. Nevertheless, the text clearly teaches that complaining to one's leaders is inappropriate and will be divinely punished.
